# ranger-base-xea2y — replaying a one-commit merge-back without the sequencer

Landed 2026-09-28, git 2.50.1 / macOS 26.4.1.

`ranger-base-tghn5` closed with its work committed on
`posse/jian-yang-posse-ranger-base-tghn5` and `main` moved on underneath it.
The launcher's replay conflicted, aborted, and filed this bead. The block's
reason named a conflict in the rebase of a single commit; what the conflict
actually WAS is the part worth keeping, because it was not in the code.

## The conflict was one add/add hunk in a GENERATED file

Read with the sweep's own operand — `git merge-tree --write-tree
--merge-base=<base> main <work>`, which is `mergesCleanly` in `worktree.go`
(`ranger-base-c6ohn`) — the whole answer was:

```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/notes.d/README.md
Auto-merging internal/posse/credential.go
```

Both sides had added one line at the head of the index's newest month heading:
`ranger-base-58qr8` on `main` (`fbf68864`), `ranger-base-tghn5` on the branch.
Neither line is anybody's hand-written text. `docs/notes.d/README.md` says so
in its own third line: *Generated by `python3 scripts/notes-index.py`; check
with `--check`.*

**So the resolution is to regenerate it, never to hand-merge it.** A
hand-merge of that hunk is a guess at the script's sort order, and it has two
ways to look right and be wrong — a file git accepts and `--check` reds
(`internal/treepins/notesindex_qa_test.go` is the pin), or, taking "ours",
one that silently drops the other bead's fragment out of the index while the
fragment file itself lands. Running the script answers both: it read the two
fragments' own dates and put `tghn5` above `58qr8`, and `--check` exits 0.

This will recur on every merge-back whose branch carries a notes fragment,
which is most of them.

## The file both sides really edited auto-merged — and that was CHECKED

`internal/posse/credential.go` is the one file on both sides of the base:
`+116/-28` from `tghn5`, `+141/-26` from `58qr8`, which is exactly where a
textually clean auto-merge can still lose a hunk. The two are related work —
`tghn5` was discovered while `58qr8` was being measured — so "it compiled" is
not evidence.

The reading that is evidence costs one command: diff the merged file against
the WORK commit, and diff that against the other side's own commit.

```
diff <(git diff --no-ext-diff <work> -- internal/posse/credential.go) \
     <(git show <main-side-commit> -- internal/posse/credential.go | sed -n '/^diff --git/,$p')
```

Identical but for blob hashes and `@@` line offsets: the merged file is
`tghn5`'s version plus exactly `58qr8`'s hunks, nothing dropped and nothing
overlapping. The two changes touch disjoint regions of a 1600-line file — the
keychain read at the top, the token shape at the bottom.

## No sequencer state was created, on purpose

AGENTS.md ("Landing the plane") warns that in a session worktree a
`cherry-pick`/`revert`/`rebase` can exit 0 and leave `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`
behind, because ending one needs the SHARED repo's `packed-refs.lock`; the
next path-limited commit then dies at `fatal: cannot do a partial commit
during a cherry-pick`, in a later call, looking like a PID refusal.

A merge-back of ONE commit does not need the sequencer at all. `merge-tree
--write-tree` already produced the merged tree in the object store, with
conflict markers written into the conflicted blob, so the replay is:

```
for p in <the commit's paths>; do git cat-file blob "$TREE:$p" > "$p"; done
```

then resolve the marked file, `git add -- <new paths>`, and commit
path-limited. No `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, no `sequencer/`, nothing to leak, and no
`git restore --worktree` either. Check first that the merged tree deletes
nothing relative to `main` (`git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only main
$TREE`) — the loop writes and adds, so a deletion in the replayed commit is
the one thing it would miss.

## Verified

`make fmt-check`, `make tree-check`, the credential suite under all three arm
tags (`internal/posse`, `-run
'Cred|Keychain|Tombstone|Composite|Seam|Shape|Runbook|GateExit|Account'`),
`scripts/notes-index.py --check`, and `make test` whole.
